page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m2.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture instance within the burstable shared server family. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor providing 16 virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores at a 2.5 GHz clock frequency. The CPU features 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and support for instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of RAM, offering 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage, relying on network-attached storage solutions, and includes a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Dedicated GPU accelerators are absent.

Benchmark measurements reflect the burstable CPU allocation profile. Single-threaded metrics show constrained output, registering 872.0 on the Geekbench single-core test and 1079.98 on stress-ng single-core execution, both falling into lower percentiles. Multi-threaded evaluations leverage the 16 virtual cores more effectively, achieving an average Geekbench multi-core score of 6459.0 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 16362.53. Memory throughput shows cached 16 KB read speeds of 1262.09 GB/sec alongside large-block uncached read and write bandwidths of 115.75 GB/sec and 60.67 GB/sec, respectively. Workload evaluations demonstrate 15.58 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 12.24 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The core tradeoff of the ecs.t5-c1m2.4xlarge lies in its burstable processing credits and absence of integrated disk storage. Because prolonged sustained CPU utilization is throttled under burstable policies, continuous heavy computation will encounter performance limits. Consequently, the instance offers cost-efficient resource provisioning primarily for intermittent batch processing, testing environments, non-critical web serving, and background ETL stages with periodic utilization patterns.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m2.4xlarge is a burstable compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY x86_64 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The system provides 16 burstable vCPUs across 8 physical cores, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio. It includes no integrated local storage and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate modest single-thread capabilities, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 872.0, while multi-threaded tasks demonstrate moderate throughput with a multi-core score of 6459.0 and 15.58 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. The absence of local disk drives requires external block storage integration. This hardware profile is appropriate for budget-sensitive, intermittent workloads such as test and staging environments, lightweight build jobs, web services with low baseline traffic, and periodic data transformation tasks.
